conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; standard Brooks setups already covered in earlier chapters (H2/L2, double bottom, moving-average gap bar, wedge, dueling lines, second entries, final flag) are only referenced here, not redefined; 'session' means one trading day of intraday bars, boundary detected by Date(0) changing

candidates.name: OpeningRangeHeightVsAverageDailyRange
candidates.quote: The opening range is about a third to half the size of the range of recent days.
candidates.description: Primitive with state: track the current session's opening-range high/low over its first N bars, and the average of the last M completed sessions' full-day range (high-low). Exposes openingRangeHeight and avgDailyRange for later candidates.
candidates.pseudocode: newSession = Date(0) != Date(1); if (newSession) { if (haveOpeningRange) pushDailyRange(sessionHigh - sessionLow); sessionHigh = high[0]; sessionLow = low[0]; barsIntoSession = 0; openingRangeSet = false } else { barsIntoSession++; sessionHigh = max(sessionHigh, high[0]); sessionLow = min(sessionLow, low[0]) } if (!openingRangeSet && barsIntoSession == openingRangeBars) { openingRangeHigh = sessionHigh; openingRangeLow = sessionLow; openingRangeHeight = openingRangeHigh - openingRangeLow; openingRangeSet = true } avgDailyRange = average(lastNDailyRanges, dayLookback)

complexity.reason: needs session-boundary detection and a rolling multi-day range history built up from intraday bars, not a plain windowed average

notes: openingRangeBars must be tuned to the bar size in use; Brooks means roughly the first one to two hours.
Page 389: 'look for a breakout and an approximate doubling of the range of the day.'

candidates.name: SmallOpeningRangePredictsExpansion
candidates.quote: If the opening range is about a third to half of the size of the recent average daily range, then look for a breakout and an approximate doubling of the range of the day.
candidates.description: Filter: the session's opening-range height is at or below a fraction of the recent average daily range, which favors a breakout later in the session and roughly a doubling of the day's range. Enables the breakout and measured-move candidates below.

complexity.reason: single comparison once T22-01's aggregates are available

candidates.name: OpeningRangeBreakoutEntry
candidates.quote: This alerted traders to a possible breakout in either direction.
candidates.description: Entry: with a small opening range in place, the current bar closes above the opening-range high; buy at the next open. Brooks prefers waiting for the breakout bar's close or the next bar's close if it is also strong, rather than buying the first tick of the break.
candidates.book_order_type: market order at (or shortly after) the close of the breakout bar

complexity.reason: reads the opening-range state from T22-01/T22-02

notes: Page 393: entering on the breakout of any trading range is called a low-probability trade in general; this is the special-case exception the book allows.

candidates.name: BreakoutPullbackPreferredEntry
candidates.quote: It is usually much better to enter on a breakout pullback or on some earlier reversal from the opposite side of the range.
candidates.description: Entry: after a close beyond the opening-range high, wait for a pullback that holds above the opening-range high, then buy when a bar closes above the pullback's signal-bar high. Preferred over the raw breakout entry (T22-03).
candidates.pseudocode: closedAboveOpeningRangeHigh(withinBars) && pullbackLow > openingRangeHigh - toleranceAtr * atr && close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the pullback's signal bar

complexity.reason: backward scan for the breakout plus a pullback-holds test

candidates.name: MeasuredMoveFromOpeningRangeTarget
candidates.quote: look for a breakout and an approximate doubling of the range of the day
candidates.description: Exit: take profit on a long entered on the opening-range breakout when price reaches the opening-range high plus the opening-range height (a measured move up projected from the breakout point).
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the measured-move target

complexity.reason: reads the remembered opening-range level and height

candidates.name: SecondRangeFormsNearMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: Once the market reaches the measured move area, it is likely to transition into a second trading range. Traders should then transition with it from trend style trading to trading range trading.
candidates.description: Research filter: once price nears the opening-range measured-move target, the with-trend breakout expectation is spent and the market is expected to consolidate into a second trading range (buy-low/sell-high, not breakout, mode). Blocks fresh with-trend breakout-style entries near the target.
candidates.pseudocode: closeTo(close[0], openingRangeHigh + moveMultiple * openingRangeHeight, nearAtrTolerance * atr)

complexity.reason: 'transition into a second trading range' is a regime judgment; the proximity-to-target proxy is a design decision

candidates.name: FadeLargeTrendBarNearMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: once the market gets close to the measured move target, bears will look for a large bull trend bar. If one forms, they will often short its close or just above its high.
candidates.description: Entry (countertrend, long side mirrored): near the opening-range measured-move target, a large trend bar prints against the day's trend; fade it, expecting an exhaustive climax and a test back into the breakout gap.
candidates.pseudocode: secondRangeFormingNearTarget && bearBody[0] && (high[0] - low[0]) >= sizeMultiple * average(high - low, rangeLookback) && close[0] < open[0]  /* long fade: buy at next open after a large bear trend bar */
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the close of the large bar, or just beyond its extreme, scaling in higher

complexity.reason: combines the researched regime filter with bar-size classification

notes: Page 392: they may scale into more as the market goes further, and exit the first entry at breakeven if the second is deeper.

candidates.name: GapTestExitTarget
candidates.quote: they will often short its close or just above its high, and then scale into more shorts if the market goes higher... they expect...an eventual test down into the gap
candidates.description: Exit for the fade in T22-07: cover once price retests the breakout gap between the first and second trading ranges (the two or three trend bars that formed the breakout).
candidates.book_order_type: limit order inside the breakout gap

complexity.reason: requires remembering the specific bars that formed the range-to-range breakout as a level

candidates.name: BreakoutTestHoldsAboveRangeIsStrength
candidates.quote: When it comes close to but does not penetrate the prior range, the trend is a little stronger.
candidates.description: Filter: after a breakout above a prior trading range, a pullback that tests down but stays above (or barely touches) that prior range's top is a sign of relative strength; favors taking further with-trend entries over countertrend ones.
candidates.pseudocode: priorRangeTop is set && low[0] >= priorRangeTop - toleranceAtr * atr && low[0] <= priorRangeTop + toleranceAtr * atr

complexity.reason: needs the prior range's boundary remembered as a level after the breakout

notes: Page 500 example: 'the bar 13 low tested the bar 7 top of the lower trading range to the tick... a sign of strength by the bulls.'

candidates.name: HigherSwingsWithinRangePredictsBreakout
candidates.quote: If you see a trading range day forming, but each swing high is a little higher than the prior one and each swing low is higher than the prior one, the market may already be trending even though it is still in a trading range.
candidates.description: Filter: while price is still confined to a trading range, the last K swing highs are each higher than the one before and the last K swing lows are each higher than the one before; this predicts an eventual upside breakout (mirrored: falling swings predict a downside breakout).
candidates.pseudocode: for k in 1..swingCount-1: swingHigh[k] > swingHigh[k+1] && swingLow[k] > swingLow[k+1]; all true

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a run test across several pivots

candidates.name: MultipleBreakoutsFavorWithTrendOnly
candidates.quote: Rarely, three or four small trading ranges will develop in a day, but when that happens, the day should probably be thought of and traded as a stronger type of trend day...Traders should focus much more if not exclusively on with-trend setups.
candidates.description: Filter: once the session has already produced at least N distinct trading-range-to-trading-range breakouts, treat the day as a strong trend day and block countertrend entries for the rest of the session.

complexity.reason: a per-session counter of a detected event (range breakout), which itself needs range/breakout detection

candidates.name: FailedOppositeSideBreakoutFade
candidates.quote: In about a third of cases, the market will break out of one side and extend the range a little, and then reverse and break out of the opposite side and extend the range a little more, resulting in a quiet trading range day.
candidates.description: Entry (fade, long side mirrored): the session already broke and extended beyond one side of the day's range by only a small amount and has now reversed to break beyond the opposite side by a small amount; buy the close of a bar that turns back up after this second, shallow breakout (expect a quiet range, not a trend).
candidates.pseudocode: shallowBreakout(oppositeSide, maxExtension) already happened this session && shallowBreakout(thisSide, maxExtension) && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: market at the close of the reversal bar

complexity.reason: needs both-direction shallow-breakout tracking within the session plus a size test on each extension

candidates.name: LateSessionReversalAfterTrendingRangeDay
candidates.quote: Since there is two-sided trading throughout the day, it is common for the day to reverse through at least one of the trading ranges in the final hour or two of the day.
candidates.description: Filter/context: on a day already classified as a trending trading range day, a countertrend reversal attempt in the final N minutes of the session is a reliable setup (retracing at least the most recent trading range), unlike earlier in the day.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter, paired with a reversal-bar entry)

complexity.reason: 'trending trading range day' classification is a design decision; the time gate itself is trivial

notes: Pairs naturally with the existing reversal-bar / two-bar-reversal entries from earlier chapters.

candidates.name: SuppressSwingLowTrailingStopInRangeRegime
candidates.quote: Traders should not trail their protective stops below a swing low once they think that the market is in a trending trading range, because those stops will usually get hit.
candidates.description: Exit-management rule: while the market is judged to be in a trending trading range, do not use a swing-low trailing stop for a long (it will typically be tagged by the two-sided swings); use a fixed or target-based exit instead.

complexity.reason: requires the same regime judgment as T22-13 plus a design decision on which exit family this toggles

candidates.name: TakeProfitOnStrengthNotWeakness
candidates.quote: It makes more sense to look to exit on strength when the market is forming an upper range, than to exit on weakness. Remember, in a trading range, traders should buy low, sell high.
candidates.description: Exit: in range regime, close a long into strength as it reaches the top of the forming upper range rather than waiting for weakness to trail it out. Practically, take profit at (or scale out into) a resistance level rather than trailing.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order near the developing range top

complexity.reason: needs a live estimate of the forming upper range's resistance level

candidates.name: PersistentSmallRangePredictsLateBreakout
candidates.quote: Every day has a range of five points at some point...Most trending trading range days with an initial range of only five points have a breakout within the first two or three hours, but several times a year the day will stay small until the final hour or two...in 90 percent of the cases the range will increase before the close.
candidates.description: Research filter: if the session's range so far, deep into the day, is still unusually small versus its own recent-day history (e.g. in the bottom couple of percentiles of the last year's daily ranges), a late-session range-expanding breakout is likely.

complexity.reason: needs a long rolling history of completed daily ranges and a percentile computation over it, plus a design decision on what counts as 'unusually small'

rejected.reason: a discretionary probability estimate with no bar-level test; not something the engine can compute or verify

rejected.quote: believing that the market had a 70 percent chance or better of at least testing their first short entry price before the close
rejected.reason: discretionary probability estimate, same as above

rejected.quote: The next day (not shown) in fact gapped up near the high of bar 7 and became a strong bull trend from the open day.

chapter_summary: Chapter 22 defines the trending trading range day: a trend built from a series of trading ranges linked by breakouts, distinguished from a spike-and-channel day mainly by weaker spikes, more overlap, and reversals that retrace whole ranges. Its distinctive, minable ideas are the opening-range-vs-average-daily-range setup and its measured-move target, the regime shift from breakout trading to range trading once that target is approached (with fades of large trend bars there and gap-test exits), signs of relative strength/weakness in how a breakout test holds, a subtle 'higher swings inside a range' early-warning clue, and management guidance (no swing-low trailing stops, exit into strength, avoid countertrend late unless in the session's final hour). Named setups it references only by name (H2/L2, double bottom, moving-average gap bar, wedge, dueling lines, final flag, second entries) are already primitives in earlier chapters and were not redefined here.
